title: A Knight and Bishop: Check the Queen Capture
summary: Compare both king captures and the corner retreat before declaring the queen exchange won.

nodes.question: Must Black recapture the bishop on c8?
nodes.explanation: No. After Bxc8+ the king can capture on c8, capture the knight on c6, or retreat to a8. Each requires a separate checked continuation.

branches.title: Source finish: the king takes the bishop
commentary: Begin after ...Qc8. White’s bishop is on d7, the knight on c6 and king on g7. Both sides’ two pawns remain on the board.
Bxc8+ captures the queen and checks Kb7 along the bishop’s diagonal. Black still has three legal king replies.
Kxc8 is the source recapture. White keeps Nc6/a5/d4 against Kc8/a6/c7, with Kg7 retained. This complete seven-piece knight ending is an exact White win.
branches.explanation: Kxc8 is the source recapture. White keeps Nc6/a5/d4 against Kc8/a6/c7, with Kg7 retained. This complete seven-piece knight ending is an exact White win.

branches.title: Independent defense: capture the knight instead
commentary: Compare a different legal king capture. The source does not illustrate this representative alternative.
Bxc8+ captures the queen with check, but does not protect Nc6.
Kxc6 captures the knight and escapes the bishop’s checking diagonal. White instead keeps Bc8/a5/d4 against Kc6/a6/c7. This distinct seven-piece bishop ending is also an exact White win.

branches.title: Independent defense: retreat to the corner
commentary: Test the legal corner retreat and complete the conversion independently of the source.
Bxc8+ removes the queen and checks Kb7.
Ka8 declines both captures. The blocked a- and c-pawns and the knight’s control of a7/b8 leave Black without a waiting move if White simply makes an irrelevant king move.
Bb7+ offers the bishop again with check. The knight still covers a7 and b8, so Black must capture the bishop.
Kxb7 is forced and reaches an exact seven-piece White win with Kg7/Nc6/a5/d4 against Kb7/a6/c7. The second sacrifice is checked as a pawn-and-knight ending rather than justified by a material count.

exercises.prompt: What are Black’s three replies to Bxc8+?
exercises.answer: Kxc8, Kxc6 and Ka8. The source shows the first; the other two are independently checked here.
It forces Kxb7 instead of making an irrelevant waiting move that would leave Black stalemated. The resulting full seven-piece knight ending is a verified White win.
